findings.title: The `http:`/`https:` scheme guard in parseAllowlistEntry is asserted by no test — all four fixtures are caught by the PATH guard instead
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Confirmed non-equivalent by inspection. All four fixtures have a non-empty, non-'/' pathname (file:///etc/passwd -> '/etc/passwd', data:text/html,<script> -> 'text/html,<script>', blob:https://admin.example/1234 -> 'https://admin.example/1234', javascript:alert(1) -> 'alert(1)'), so with the scheme throw deleted every one still throws AdminOriginConfigError from the path throw two guards later. The mutant is observably different: readAdminAppOrigins() returns ['ftp://admin.example'] / ['null'] instead of throwing for entries whose pathname is '/' (ftp://, ws://, wss://, file://host) — that is an exported-function behaviour change, so 'equivalent' cannot be claimed. Not an unexecuted branch: the test DOES run the scheme guard, its assertion simply cannot distinguish which guard fired. Security impact is nil today because normalizeOrigin independently enforces http(s) on the request side, so no extra origin becomes admissible; the defect is in the ORACLE. One-line fix: add an entry whose ONLY disqualifier is the scheme (e.g. 'ftp://admin.example' or 'ws://admin.example') to the fixture list.

findings.title: The Edge-safety guard's `node:` entry can never match, and side-effect imports are invisible — both node-builtin import shapes survive
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Confirmed non-equivalent and semantically meaningful. The membership test is `s === bad || s.startsWith(`${bad}/`)`; for bad='node:' that demands the specifier be exactly 'node:' or start with 'node:/', neither of which is a real specifier, so 'node:crypto' passes (M27 survived). Separately the extractor is /from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g, so a bare `import 'node:crypto';` yields no specifier at all (M28 survived). The 'node builtins' third of the test's stated property is enforced by nothing, which is the exact hole the cited precedent (src/lib/auth/__tests__/admin-transport.test.ts:114-119) documents a prior red-team pass walking through twice. The '@/lib/db', 'postgres', 'bullmq', 'openai', '@anthropic-ai/sdk', '@supabase/supabase-js' and 'ioredis' entries DO match and are unaffected. No live defect: the graph carries no node: import at HEAD. Fix: special-case the scheme (s.startsWith('node:')) and widen the extractor to /(?:from|import)\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g.

findings.title: Fix 1's fail-closed fallback keys on VERCEL, which Vercel documents as the marker that system environment variables ARE exposed - so in the exact configuration A1 describes the predicate still returns false
findings.arbiter_reasoning:
Duty 3, re-resolved this pass against vercel.com/docs/environment-variables/system-environment-variables via the Vercel documentation MCP: 'VERCEL environment variable - Indicates that system environment variables are exposed to the deployment. VERCEL=1'. VERCEL is itself a system environment variable and its documented meaning is that the exposure toggle is ON. A1's scenario is a project whose system variables are NOT exposed; there VERCEL_TARGET_ENV is absent AND VERCEL is absent, so process.env.VERCEL !== undefined is false and isProductionEnvironment() returns false - http://localhost:<any port> stays admissible on a real production deployment, which is the hole the fix was written to close. Two consequences, both checked. (a) NO REGRESSION: the new predicate returns exactly what the old one returned in every configuration where the fallback runs, and R14/R15/R16/R17 all killed, so the shipped behaviour is unchanged and correctly pinned. (b) The CLAIM is what fails: the JSDoc at src/lib/config/flags.ts:57-62 ('on Vercel with the signal switched off - treat as production') and triage.md:37's A1 disposition both assert a property the marker cannot deliver. Rated P1 not P0 because the evidence is vendor documentation rather than a probe of this project's own deployment, and because nothing regressed. Blast radius checked and small: isAllowedAdminOrigin's loopback clause (src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts:188) is the ONLY caller in the repo. Local dev, pnpm test and the Railway worker are unaffected - VERCEL is unset in all three, and the repo runs next dev, never vercel dev (no occurrence of 'vercel dev' outside node_modules). Remedy: verify live the way src/lib/config/deployment-lane.ts:5-10 verified the Railway signals ('Verified live against Railway on 2026-07-28'), or key the fallback on something that survives the toggle. If this project's toggle is ON - the default - the fallback is dead code and A1 was hypothetical here; say that instead of claiming a fix.

--- ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (post round 2) ---
FIXED at 1ded393a+1. The fallback no longer keys on VERCEL — which is itself a system environment variable meaning 'system variables ARE exposed', so it is absent in exactly the configuration the fallback exists for. It now keys on NODE_ENV === 'production', which is true on every Vercel build, so the A1 hole is genuinely closed. The imprecision (staging builds also set NODE_ENV=production) is reached ONLY when VERCEL_TARGET_ENV is missing and errs toward DENYING loopback; an affirmative target still beats it, which the new test cases pin (staging + preview under NODE_ENV=production stay non-production).

Fix 1 added 'delete process.env.VERCEL' to admin-origins.test.ts's withEnv (:37) with the reason that 'leaving a stray VERCEL in the environment would silently make every lane read as production', and to flags.test.ts (:71). proxy.test.ts's beforeEach was not updated. No assertion depends on it TODAY - both loopback proxy cases set VERCEL_TARGET_ENV explicitly ('staging' at :439, 'production' at :450), an affirmative signal that short-circuits the new fallback - so this is P2 and no test is currently fragile. It becomes a live hazard the moment a loopback case is added without setting the target env: the suite would then pass or fail on whether the developer's shell exports VERCEL. One-line remedy, matching the two sibling suites.

--- ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (post round 2) ---
FIXED, by removal of the cause. The proxy suite's beforeEach no longer needs to clear VERCEL because isProductionEnvironment stopped reading it (RT-10). NODE_ENV is 'test' under vitest, so the default lane is non-production and the loopback cases hold.

findings.title: The catch's non-AdminOriginConfigError rethrow is unreachable at HEAD and exercised by no test
findings.arbiter_reasoning:
Duty 1, uncovered defensive branch. R12 deletes the rethrow so the catch swallows every error, and the covering test still passes (INV-212). Recorded as equivalent rather than a survivor because the mutant is PROVABLY behaviour-preserving at HEAD: readAdminAppOrigins() reaches only process.env, String split/map/filter/trim, parseAllowlistEntry (which throws AdminOriginConfigError alone) and url.origin, and parseUrl catches new URL() - so every error that can arrive at the catch already IS an AdminOriginConfigError. The rethrow is correct defensive depth for a future in which that stops being true. Filed so the arbiter knows nothing measures it; no action recommended, since a test would mean stubbing a module that cannot fail.

--- ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (post round 2) ---
REJECTED — kept deliberately. The rethrow of a non-AdminOriginConfigError is unreachable at HEAD, and that is the point: it is the 'assert impossible states' rule, not defensive handling. Swallowing an unexpected error into a 403 origin would hide a real fault behind a CORS refusal. Being unmeasured is the correct condition for an assertion that must never fire.
